name: Split-Strike Synthetic Long (Risk Reversal)
summary: Sell an OTM put and buy an OTM call in the same expiry for near-zero net cost, giving stock-like upside above the call strike and stock-like downside below the put strike with a flat zone between.

legs.strike_rule: OTM put at delta -0.25 to -0.30 (choose the listed strike whose delta is nearest -0.27)
OTM call at delta +0.25 to +0.30, i.e. roughly symmetric around spot

max_profit: UNDEFINED (unlimited) above the call strike: (spot_at_exit - call_strike) x 100 - net_debit
max_loss: (put_strike x 100) - net_credit if the underlying goes to zero

greeks.delta: +0.50 to +0.60 at entry, rising toward +1.00 as spot moves outside either strike
greeks.gamma: near zero at spot, positive above the call strike, negative below the put strike
greeks.theta: slightly positive when opened for a credit with symmetric deltas; the short put usually decays faster
greeks.vega: slightly negative on a standard equity skew (the put sold carries more IV than the call bought) — this is the skew trade embedded in the structure

breakevens: Upside: call_strike + net_debit/100. Downside: put_strike - net_credit/100. Between the strikes the P/L equals the net credit or debit.
when_to_use: Bullish view financed by selling downside skew. Best when IV rank > 40 and put skew is steep (25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV > 4 vol points), because the sold put is then genuinely expensive relative to the bought call.
entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: the short put is uncovered. Requires Level 4.

Level-3-legal substitute: replace the naked short put with a put credit spread (put_strike and put_strike - width), producing a defined-risk 'risk reversal with a floor'. That variant IS Level 3 legal and should be the router's fallback.
If ever run at Level 4: open only for a net credit or a net debit <= $0.25, and only when 25d put IV - 25d call IV >= 4.0 vol points.
Both strikes must be roughly delta-symmetric: |put_delta| and call_delta must be within 0.05 of each other.
Underlying price >= $20, 20-day ADV >= 2,000,000 shares, OI >= 500 per leg.
No entry within 2 sessions of earnings or 5 days of an ex-dividend date.
management_rules: Close at 50% of the maximum realistic gain measured as (current package mark - entry mark) >= 0.50 x (call_strike - spot_at_entry), or at 21 DTE, whichever comes first.
Hard stop: close if the package loses 2.0x the net credit received, or 100% of the net debit paid.
If the short put delta reaches -0.45, either close the whole structure or roll the put down-and-out one expiry for a credit; never roll for a debit.
Do not adjust the long call independently; the structure's whole point is the paired skew.
exit_rules: MANDATORY ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short put no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
If spot < put_strike at any point on expiration day, close the short put by 14:00 ET.
At 21 DTE, if the short put is ITM, close the structure entirely rather than carrying it.
If the long call expires worthless and the short put is OTM by more than 5%, the position may be allowed to lapse — but only after a 15:40 ET confirmation that the put is OTM; when in doubt, close.
assignment_risk: On the short put only. Early assignment on an OTM put is effectively zero; risk appears when the underlying falls through the put strike and the put's extrinsic value decays below ~$0.05. Assignment delivers 100 long shares at the put strike, tying up (put_strike x 100) of capital. The long call cannot offset this.
buying_power: Naked short put Reg T requirement (roughly 20% of underlying value less OTM amount plus premium), less the long call's debit. Typically $1,200-$2,000 per contract on a $100 name.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 per leg, package bid-ask <= $0.10. Wing strikes on illiquid names quote very wide and destroy the near-zero-cost premise.
common_mistakes: Chasing 'zero cost' by widening the call strike until the credit balances — this quietly moves the structure to a much worse risk/reward. Also ignoring that the short put is the entire risk of the trade while attention stays on the long call.
zero_dte_notes: Skew is unstable and gamma is enormous at 0DTE; the short put can go from -0.10 delta to assigned within one session.
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
